newsitem.title: USA: MAPCO, Texaco set Discovery work.
newsitem.headline: MAPCO, Texaco set Discovery work.

text.p: MAPCO Inc said Tuesday construction of the Discovery Pipeline in the Gulf of Mexico will begin in mid-March after all the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission required conditions have been satisfied.

The 30-inch, 150-mile natural gas pipeline will access deepwater exploration taking place in the central Gulf of Mexico, specifically in the South Timbalier, Grand Isle, Ewing Bank, Green Canyon and Mississippi Canyon areas offshore Louisiana. It is part of the $300 million Discovery project being developed jointly by MAPCO and Texaco Inc.
The Discovery partners anticipate the pipeline will begin accepting gas in the fourth quarter of 1997, MAPCO said.

In addition to this pipeline, the project includes construction of a cryogenic processing plant capable of processing 650 million cubic feet of natural gas per day and an upgrade of a natural gas liquids fractionator in Paradis, La., giving it a capacity of 42,000 barrels per day.
Work on the gas processing plant and the fractionator upgrade has already begun, MAPCO said.
